name: Amaimon
confidence_why: The only description of Amaimon, the three-page SIL phonology data sheet checked by Lillie (2001), says stress does not seem to be phonemic and never states where it falls, and neither Z'graggen (1975) nor Pick (2020) says anything about stress, so the record rests on one uncontradicted first-hand source.

catalog_locator: OPD section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', p. 2 (the only stress statement in the document)
catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress does not seem to be phonemic. Tone and length are not found.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened 133,960 B, 3 pp., text, the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Microsoft Word - Amaimon_ali') and ran extracted text per page: page 2 lines 42-44 read exactly 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic. Tone and length are not found.' -- verbatim as quoted, locator p. 2 correct. Surrounding content (p.1 inventory, consonant/vowel examples; p.2 diphthongs, suprasegmentals, syllable patterns V/CV/CVV/CVC/CVVC/VC; p.3 hawk text) contains no other stress statement, no placement rule, no stress marks in the example transcriptions. Header p.1: 'Amaimon (Mabulap) Language [ALI] Tebesarik - Madang Province', villages Tebesarik, Wagusarik, Koromasarik, Amaimo…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record for Amaimon has an empty rule and there are no existing statements; this OPD supplies the only stress statement found: stress is judged non-phonemic (i.e. predictable), but the sheet does not say where it falls, and tone and length are stated to be absent. Compatible with the (empty) catalog entry and adds the non-contrastive finding; no placement to agree or disagree with.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is not contrastive in Amaimon (placement not specified); the language has neither tone nor contrastive vowel length, per a 2-week SIL workshop data sheet checked by P. Lillie in 2001.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is hedged ('does not seem to be').
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD identifies the variety as 'Amaimon (Mabulap) Language [ALI]', villages Tebesarik, Wagusarik, Koromasarik, Amaimon (Madang Province); the AP1-044 recording is of speaker Janet Angal, village not stated on the item page.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in the OPD text we hold at the stated place; it is the document's only suprasegmental sentence and no example carries stress marks, so not determinable (non-phonemic stress asserted, position never stated) is the faithful code. (2) The deciding source is a 3-page unreviewed SIL workshop data sheet (2001) — minimal, but every catalogue I could open (Glottolog 5.1 bib: 3 Z'graggen survey items, 0 descriptive refs; SIL archive: 1 item; OLAC 2025: OPD + audio deposits only) and Pick 2020 p. 203 ('available data.. very limited', citing only Lillie 2001) show it is the only written phonological statement on Amaimon. Z'graggen 1971 (held) explicitly omits stress for the whole Madang survey; Z'graggen 1975 PL C-38 (downloaded now, p. 584) and 1980 PL D-31 (held) are silent.
